headline: Highest risk is data leakage: RD-Agent’s broad egress and API use can expose shared inputs, while the awesome-list profile has no isolation or runtime controls to contain interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime surfaces beyond being a docs-only open-source list, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs by default. B can run browsers and process external content, but A does not provide a shared channel or parser. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore limited to unusual manual copy/paste or external orchestration, not a default bridge.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into A-associated workflows, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between them, A can receive attacker-controlled content.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting B outputs into A-related docs without review.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared queue integration.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags before any cross-agent handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B touches financial reports, datasets, logs, and has broad network egress plus API calls. If the pair shares inputs through files or orchestration, B can transmit those contents off-box. The leakage pathway is not proven by a shared workspace, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF A is given sensitive files that B can read from a shared workspace, B may exfiltrate them via API calls.
IF B is configured with live credentials and receives A-produced artifacts, those artifacts can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Store A and B in separate directories.
Do not place secrets or regulated data in any shared folder.
Run B with outbound network blocked for test runs.
Rotate any API keys used by B before production use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or mutable-resource permissions documented, so it cannot conflict materially with B’s broad API and file activity. B supports multiple instances and writes logs, but without overlapping writable surfaces from A there is no strong write-write conflict. The remaining risk is limited to coordination mistakes if an external orchestrator adds shared state.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, log or file collisions can occur.
IF an orchestrator gives A mutable access not shown in its profile, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Serialize any shared writes through one coordinator.
Keep A read-only.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated list and does not generate operational facts, while B is an automated research agent that can act on inputs and produce logs, papers, and execution traces. If B treats A-derived recommendations as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream research outputs. Because A is not a live reasoning agent, the pathway is indirect and not high severity.
conditions: IF B consumes A-curated recommendations without verification, incorrect guidance can propagate into reports or traces.
IF an operator uses A as a source of truth for B’s task planning, B may act on stale or incomplete information.
mitigations: Require B to verify any A-derived claim against primary sources.
Mark A as reference-only in the workflow.
Add a human review step before B publishes outputs.
requires-engineering: add citation checks in B’s pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source docs artifact with no touched data classes, while B explicitly handles financial reports, logs, and competition datasets and uses third-party APIs. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated data is routed into B’s cloud-backed workflow. A is not cited for residency because it has no data handling surface; the risk is driven by B’s documented processing model.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated financial records are processed by B without a DPA, compliance exposure increases.
IF B logs sensitive inputs into log/ and those logs are retained beyond policy, retention obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into B until legal review is complete.
Review B’s logging and retention settings.
Use synthetic or anonymized datasets for B.
Restrict API keys to non-production scopes.
requires-engineering: document a DPA and residency control for B.
